newsitem.title: USA: Rains delay Texas rice planting, yield may be down.
newsitem.headline: Rains delay Texas rice planting, yield may be down.

text.p: Intermittent rainfall from late February to April delayed Texas rice plantings, which may lead to yield losses, said Jim Stansel, research director of the Texas Agricultural Research and Extension Center, Beaumont, Texas.

"Late planting is associated with increased disease and insect pressure and less available sunlight. It also increases the probability of damage from weather such as hurricane or thunderstorms," Stansel told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He also noted late harvesting in August can affect milling quality and decrease the likelihood of a ratoon or second crop.
"As of May 5, only 48 percent or about 120,000 acres have been planted to Texas riceland, down from 98 percent planted or 253,000 acres planted during the same year-ago period," Stansel said.

Texas, which ranks fourth in U.S. states for rice output, produced about 18.5 million hundredweight (cwt) last year, the U.S. Department of Agriculture said. Stansel said he expected Texas to produce 13 million cwt this year due to the weather-delayed plantings.
